title.zh: 卷七十四 志第五十 職官三
title.raw: 卷七十四 志第五十 職官三 Volume 74 Treatises 50: Official Posts 3

sentences.zh: 太常寺附提督四夷館光祿寺太僕寺鴻臚寺尚寶司六科中書舍人行人司欽天監太醫院上林苑監五城兵馬司順天府附宛平大興二縣武學僧道錄司教坊司宦官女官

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with appended sections on the Supervisor of the Four Barbarian Translation Offices, Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Stud, Court of State Ceremonial, Imperial Seals Office, Six Offices of Scrutiny, Palace Secretariat Drafters, Reception Office, Directorate of Astronomy, Imperial Medical Institute, Directorate of the Imperial Parks, Five-City Military Patrol Office, Shuntian Prefecture with appended Wanping and Daxing counties, Military Academy, Office for Recording Buddhist and Taoist Affairs, Office of the Imperial Music Bureau, eunuchs, and palace women.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with appended sections on the Supervisor of the Four Barbarian Translation Offices, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, the Court of the Imperial Stud, the Court of State Ceremonial, the Imperial Seals Office, the Six Offices of Scrutiny, Palace Secretariat Drafters, the Reception Office, the Directorate of Astronomy, the Imperial Medical Institute, the Directorate of the Imperial Parks, the Five-City Military Patrol Office, Shuntian Prefecture (with Wanping and Daxing counties), the Military Academy, the Office for Recording Buddhist and Taoist Affairs, the Office of the Imperial Music Bureau, eunuchs, and palace women.

sentences.zh: 太常寺。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 卿一人，正三品少卿二人，正四品寺丞二人。

translations.literal: One Director, rank 3a; two Vice Directors, rank 4a; two Assistant Directors.
translations.idiomatic: One Director at rank 3a; two Vice Directors at rank 4a; and two Assistant Directors.

sentences.zh: 正六品其屬，典簿廳，典簿二人，正七品博士二人，協律郎二人，正八品，嘉靖中增至五人。

translations.literal: Rank 6a subordinates: the Registry, with two Registrars at rank 7a; two Doctors at rank 7a; two Masters of Harmonics at rank 8b—in the Jiajing reign increased to five.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates at rank 6a included a Registry with two Registrars at rank 7a, two Doctors at rank 7a, and two Masters of Harmonics at rank 8b; under the Jiajing emperor the latter post was raised to five.

sentences.zh: 贊禮郎九人，正九品，嘉靖中增至三十三人，後革二人。

translations.literal: Nine Masters of Ceremonial at rank 9a—in the Jiajing reign increased to thirty-three, later reduced by two.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Masters of Ceremonial at rank 9a; under Jiajing the number rose to thirty-three, then two posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 司樂二十人。

translations.literal: Twenty Directors of Music.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty Directors of Music.

sentences.zh: 從九品，嘉靖中增至三十九人，後革五人。

translations.literal: Rank 9b—in the Jiajing reign increased to thirty-nine, later reduced by five.
translations.idiomatic: At rank 9b; under Jiajing the corps grew to thirty-nine, then five posts were cut.

sentences.zh: 天壇、地壇、朝日壇、夕月壇、先農壇、帝王廟、祈穀殿、長陵、獻陵、景陵、裕陵、茂陵、泰陵、顯陵、康陵、永陵、昭陵各祠祭署，俱奉祀一人，從七品祀丞二人。

translations.literal: For the Altars of Heaven and Earth, the Altars of the Rising Sun and Setting Moon, the Altar of the First Farmer, the Temple of Former Emperors, the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, and the mausoleums of Chang, Xian, Jing, Yu, Mao, Tai, Xian, Kang, Yong, and Zhao—each Sacrificial Office had one Sacrificial Officer at rank 7b and two Assistant Sacrificial Officers at rank 8b.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial offices at the Altars of Heaven and Earth, the Rising Sun and Setting Moon altars, the Altar of the First Farmer, the Temple of Former Emperors, the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, and the Chang, Xian, Jing, Yu, Mao, Tai, Xian, Kang, Yong, and Zhao mausoleums each had one Sacrificial Officer at rank 7b and two Assistant Sacrificial Officers at rank 8b.

sentences.zh: 從八品犧牲所，吏目一人。

translations.literal: The Office of Sacrificial Victims, with one Clerk at rank 8b.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Sacrificial Victims had one Clerk at rank 8b.

sentences.zh: 從九品

translations.literal: rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: at rank 9b.

sentences.zh: 太常，掌祭祀禮樂之事，總其官屬，籍其政令，以聽於禮部。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices oversaw sacrificial rites and ritual music, directed its subordinates, kept records of its regulations, and reported to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The court oversaw state sacrifices and ritual music, directed its staff, registered its regulations, and took direction from the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 凡天神、地祇、人鬼，歲祭有常。

translations.literal: For spirits of Heaven, Earth, and the dead, annual sacrifices followed fixed schedules.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices to heavenly, earthly, and human spirits followed a fixed annual calendar.

sentences.zh: 先冬十二月朔，奏進明年祭日，天子禦奉天殿受之，乃頒於諸司。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, the court submitted the coming year's sacrificial calendar; the Son of Heaven received it in the Hall of Supreme Harmony and then distributed it to the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month the court submitted the next year's sacrificial calendar; the emperor received it in the Hall of Supreme Harmony and had it promulgated to all departments.

sentences.zh: 天子親祭，則贊相禮儀。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven performed sacrifices in person, the court assisted with the ritual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sacrificed in person, its officers guided the ceremonial proceedings.

sentences.zh: 大臣攝事，亦如之。

translations.literal: When a senior minister acted on the emperor's behalf, the court did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied when a senior minister stood in for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 凡國有冊立、冊封、冠婚、營繕、徵討、大喪諸典禮，歲時旱澇大災變，則請告宗廟社稷。

translations.literal: For state events such as investiture, enfeoffment, capping and marriage, construction, campaigns, and major mourning, and for severe drought, flood, or other calamities of the season, memorials were presented to the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Investitures, enfeoffments, capping and weddings, construction projects, military campaigns, state mourning, and severe seasonal droughts, floods, or other disasters all required notification at the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 薦新則移光祿寺供其品物。

translations.literal: For offerings of new harvest, the Court of Imperial Entertainments was instructed to supply the requisite items.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal offerings of new harvest were arranged through the Court of Imperial Entertainments for the requisite provisions.

sentences.zh: 祭祀先期請省牲，進祝版、銅人，上殿奏請齋戒，親署御名。

translations.literal: Before sacrifices, the court requested inspection of victims, submitted prayer boards and bronze figures, entered the hall to memorialize on fasting and purification, and had the emperor sign his name in person.
translations.idiomatic: Before each sacrifice it arranged inspection of the victims, submitted prayer boards and bronze ritual figures, memorialized in hall on the emperor's fast, and secured his personal signature on the documents.

sentences.zh: 省牲偕光祿卿。

translations.literal: Inspection of victims was conducted jointly with the Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Victim inspection was carried out together with the Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 惟大祀車駕親省，大臣日一省之。

translations.literal: Only for major sacrifices did the imperial carriage attend inspection in person; otherwise a senior minister inspected once daily.
translations.idiomatic: For major sacrifices the emperor went in person to inspect the victims; otherwise a senior minister inspected them once a day.

sentences.zh: 凡祭，滌器、爨埋、香燭、玉帛，整拂神幄，必恭潔。

translations.literal: For every sacrifice: cleansing vessels, cooking and burial offerings, incense and candles, jade and silk—all with careful arrangement of the spirit curtains, always with reverence and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Every sacrifice required cleansing vessels, preparing cooked and buried offerings, incense and candles, and jade and silk, with the spirit curtains arranged scrupulously in reverent cleanliness.

sentences.zh: 掌燎、看燎、讀祝、奏禮、對引、司香、進俎、舉麾、陳設、收支、導引、設位、典儀、通贊、奉帛、執爵、司樽、司罍洗，卿貳屬各領其事，罔有不共。

translations.literal: Managing the flame, watching the flame, reading prayers, presenting ritual, paired guidance, tending incense, presenting meat trays, raising banners, arranging offerings, receiving and disbursing, leading processions, setting positions, directing ceremony, general acclamation, presenting silk, holding goblets, tending wine vessels, and washing vessels—the Director, Vice Directors, and subordinates each led their duties; none failed to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Posts from flame-tending and prayer-reading through incense, meat trays, banners, offerings, processions, acclamation, silk and goblets, wine vessels, and washing were each assigned to the Director, Vice Directors, or their staff, and all took part without exception.

sentences.zh: 凡玉四等：曰蒼璧，以祀天曰黃琮，以祀地曰赤璋、白琥，以朝日、夕月曰兩圭有邸。

translations.literal: Jade came in four grades: the green disc for Heaven; the yellow cube for Earth; the red tablet and white tiger-shaped piece for the Rising Sun and Setting Moon; the paired scepters with pedestals for the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: There were four grades of jade: the green disc for Heaven, the yellow cube for Earth, red tablet and white tiger-piece for the sun and moon altars, and paired scepters with pedestals for the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 以祭太社、太稷帛五等：曰郊祀制帛，祀天地曰奉先制帛，薦祖考曰禮神制帛，祭社稷、羣神、帝王、先師曰展親制帛，祭享親王曰報功制帛，祭享功臣。

translations.literal: for sacrifices at the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain. Silk came in five grades: suburban-sacrifice silk for Heaven and Earth; ancestral silk for offering to forebears; spirit-worship silk for the altars of soil and grain, collective spirits, former emperors, and the Sage; kinship silk for sacrifices to imperial princes; merit silk for sacrifices to meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Silk came in five grades: suburban-sacrifice silk for Heaven and Earth; ancestral silk for forebears; spirit-worship silk for the altars of soil and grain, collective spirits, former emperors, and the Sage; kinship silk for imperial princes; and merit silk for meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 牲四等：曰犢，曰牛，曰太牢，曰少牢。

translations.literal: Victims came in four grades: calf, ox, grand victim set, and lesser victim set.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial victims came in four grades: calf, ox, the grand victim set, and the lesser victim set.

sentences.zh: 色尚騂或黝。

translations.literal: Color favored reddish-brown or dark.
translations.idiomatic: Preferred colors were reddish-brown or dark.

sentences.zh: 大祀入滌三月，中祀一月，小祀一旬。

translations.literal: Major sacrifices required three months of purification; medium sacrifices one month; minor sacrifices ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Major sacrifices required three months of victim purification, medium sacrifices one month, and minor sacrifices ten days.

sentences.zh: 樂四等：曰九奏，用祀天地曰八奏，神祇、太歲，曰七奏，大明、太社、太稷、帝王曰六奏。

translations.literal: Music came in four grades: nine movements for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth; eight for spirits and the Year Star; seven for the Bright Luminary, Grand Altars of Soil and Grain, and former emperors; six for
translations.idiomatic: Music had four grades: nine movements for Heaven and Earth; eight for spirits and the Year Star; seven for the Bright Luminary, the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain, and former emperors; six for

sentences.zh: 夜明、帝社、帝稷、宗廟、先師。

translations.literal: the Night Brightener, Imperial Altars of Soil and Grain, ancestral temple, and the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: the Night Brightener, the Imperial Altars of Soil and Grain, the ancestral temple, and the Sage.

sentences.zh: 舞二：曰文舞，曰武舞。

translations.literal: Dance came in two forms: civil dance and martial dance.
translations.idiomatic: There were two dances: the civil dance and the martial dance.

sentences.zh: 樂器不徙。

translations.literal: Musical instruments were not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Musical instruments were not relocated.

sentences.zh: 陵園之祭無樂。

translations.literal: Sacrifices at imperial mausoleums had no music.
translations.idiomatic: Mausoleum sacrifices were performed without music.

sentences.zh: 歲終合祭五禮之神，則少卿攝事。

translations.literal: At year's end, when the spirits of the five rites were sacrificed to collectively, a Vice Director acted on behalf of the Director.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end, for the collective sacrifice to the spirits of the five rites, a Vice Director stood in for the Director.

sentences.zh: 初，吳元年置太常司，設卿，正三品少卿，正四品丞，正五品典簿、協律郎、博士，正七品贊禮郎。

translations.literal: Originally, in the first year of the Wu reign era the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was established as a bureau, with a Director at rank 3a, Vice Director at rank 4a, Assistant Director at rank 5a, Registrar, Master of Harmonics, and Doctor at rank 7a, and Master of Ceremonial at rank 7a.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu era the bureau was established with a Director at rank 3a, Vice Director at 4a, Assistant Director at 5a, and Registrars, Masters of Harmonics, Doctors, and Masters of Ceremonial at rank 7a.

sentences.zh: 從八品洪武初，置各祠祭署，設署令、署丞。

translations.literal: rank 8b. At the beginning of Hongwu, various Sacrificial Offices were established, each with an Office Director and Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: at rank 8b. Early in Hongwu various sacrificial offices were set up, each with a director and deputy.

sentences.zh: 十三年，更定協律郎等官品秩。

translations.literal: In year 13, the ranks of Masters of Harmonics and related posts were revised.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 the ranks of the Masters of Harmonics and related posts were fixed anew.

sentences.zh: 協律郎正八品，贊禮郎正九品，司樂從九品。

translations.literal: Master of Harmonics at rank 8b; Master of Ceremonial at rank 9a; Director of Music at rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Harmonics was rank 8b, the Master of Ceremonial rank 9a, and the Director of Music rank 9b.

sentences.zh: 三十四年改各署令為奉祀，署丞為祀丞。

translations.literal: In year 34, Office Directors were renamed Sacrificial Officers and Assistant Directors renamed Assistant Sacrificial Officers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 34 office directors were retitled Sacrificial Officers and their deputies Assistant Sacrificial Officers.

sentences.zh: 二十年改司為寺，官制仍舊。

translations.literal: In year 20 the bureau was renamed a court; the official structure remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 the bureau became a court, but the establishment of posts was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十五年已定司丞正六品。

translations.literal: In year 25 the Assistant Director's rank of 6a had already been fixed.
translations.idiomatic: By year 25 the Assistant Director's rank of 6a was already established.

sentences.zh: 建文中，增設贊禮郎二人，太祝一人，以及各祠祭署俱有更革。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, two Masters of Ceremonial and one Grand Sacrificer were added, and all Sacrificial Offices underwent further changes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen two Masters of Ceremonial and one Grand Sacrificer were added, and every sacrificial office was reorganized.

sentences.zh: 天壇祠祭署為南郊祠祭署，泗州祠祭署為泗濱祠祭署，宿州祠祭署為新豐祠祭署，孝陵置鐘山祠祭署，各司圃所增神樂觀知觀一人。

translations.literal: The Altar of Heaven Sacrificial Office became the Southern Suburb Sacrificial Office; the Sizhou office became the Sibin Sacrificial Office; the Suzhou office became the Xinfeng Sacrificial Office; a Zhongshan Sacrificial Office was established for the Xiaoling mausoleum; and each park office added one Superintendent of the Divine Music Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: The Heaven Altar office was renamed for the southern suburb; Sizhou's office became Sibin; Suzhou's became Xinfeng; a Zhongshan office was set up for the Xiaoling mausoleum; and each imperial park added a superintendent for the Divine Music Observatory.

sentences.zh: 成祖初，惟易天壇為天地壇，餘悉復洪武間制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongle reign, only the Altar of Heaven was changed to the Altar of Heaven and Earth; everything else reverted to the Hongwu system.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle only the Heaven Altar was merged into a Heaven-and-Earth altar; all else reverted to Hongwu practice.

sentences.zh: 建文時，南郊祠祭署為郊壇祠祭署，已又改為天地壇祠祭署。

translations.literal: Under Jianwen the Southern Suburb Sacrificial Office had become the Suburban Altar Sacrificial Office, and was then changed again to the Heaven-and-Earth Altar Sacrificial Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen the southern-suburb office had briefly become the suburban-altar office, then the heaven-and-earth altar office.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年置犧牲所，吏目典掌文移。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi the Office of Sacrificial Victims was established, with a Clerk in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxi year 1 saw the Office of Sacrificial Victims established, with a clerk handling its paperwork.

sentences.zh: 先是，洪武三年置神牲所，設廩牲令、大使、副使等官。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Hongwu year 3 the Divine Victims Office had been established, with posts of Victim Granary Director, Chief Envoy, and Vice Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Hongwu year 3, a Divine Victims Office had been set up with a granary director, chief envoy, and vice envoy.

sentences.zh: 四年革。

translations.literal: In year 4 it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in year 4.

sentences.zh: 世宗釐祀典，分天地壇為天壇、地壇，山川壇、耤田祠祭署為神祇壇，大祀殿為祈穀殿，增置朝日、夕月二壇，各設祠祭署。

translations.literal: The Shizong emperor reformed the sacrificial canon: the Heaven-and-Earth Altar was split into separate Altars of Heaven and Earth; the Mountains-and-Rivers Altar and Plough-Field Sacrificial Office became the Altar of Spirits; the Grand Sacrifice Hall became the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests; and the Rising Sun and Setting Moon altars were added, each with its own Sacrificial Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong reformed the ritual code: the combined heaven-and-earth altar was split; the mountains-and-rivers and plough-field offices became the Spirits altar; the Grand Sacrifice Hall became the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests; and new Rising Sun and Setting Moon altars each received a sacrificial office.

sentences.zh: 又增設協律郎、贊禮郎、司樂等員。

translations.literal: Additional posts of Master of Harmonics, Master of Ceremonial, Director of Music, and others were also established.
translations.idiomatic: He also increased the numbers of Masters of Harmonics, Masters of Ceremonial, Directors of Music, and related posts.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，革協律郎等官四十八員，萬曆六年復設，如嘉靖間制。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing, forty-eight posts including Masters of Harmonics were abolished; in the sixth year of Wanli they were restored as under the Jiajing system.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing year 3 cut forty-eight such posts; Wanli year 6 restored them to the Jiajing establishment.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年，改神祇壇為先農壇。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wanli the Altar of Spirits was renamed the Altar of the First Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli year 4 renamed the Spirits altar the Altar of the First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 提督四夷館。

translations.literal: The Supervisor of the Four Barbarian Translation Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervisor of the Four Barbarian Translation Offices.

sentences.zh: 少卿一人，正四品掌譯書之事。

translations.literal: One Vice Director at rank 4a, in charge of translation work.
translations.idiomatic: One Vice Director at rank 4a oversaw translation work.

sentences.zh: 自永樂五年，外國朝貢，特設蒙古、女直、西番、西天、回回、百夷、高昌、緬甸八館，置譯字生、通事，通事初隸通政使司通譯語言文字。

translations.literal: From the fifth year of Yongle, as foreign states came to court with tribute, eight offices were specially established—for Mongol, Jurchen, Tibetan, Indian, Muslim, Bai, Gaochang, and Burmese—with Translation Students and Interpreters; Interpreters were initially subordinate to the Office of Transmission for oral and written translation.
translations.idiomatic: From Yongle year 5, as tribute missions multiplied, eight translation bureaus were set up—for Mongol, Jurchen, Tibetan, Indian, Muslim, Bai, Gaochang, and Burmese—staffed with translation students and interpreters; interpreters initially reported to the Office of Transmission for spoken and written translation.

sentences.zh: 正德中，增設八百館。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign a Lanna bureau was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde a Lanna bureau was added.

sentences.zh: 八百國蘭者哥進貢萬曆中，又增設暹羅館。

translations.literal: When the Lanna state of Lan Na Ko presented tribute, and during the Wanli reign a Siamese bureau was also added.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Na Ko of the Lanna states sent tribute, and under Wanli a Siamese bureau was added as well.

sentences.zh: 初設四夷館隸翰林院，選國子監生習譯。

translations.literal: When first established the Four Barbarian Translation Offices were subordinate to the Hanlin Academy; students from the Imperial Academy were selected to study translation.
translations.idiomatic: At first the translation offices came under the Hanlin Academy, which selected Imperial Academy students for language training.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，兼選官民子弟，委官教肄，學士稽考程課。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, sons of officials and commoners were also selected; officials were appointed to instruct them, and academicians examined their progress.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande year 1 broadened recruitment to officials' and commoners' sons, with assigned instructors and Hanlin academicians grading their progress.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年，始增設太常寺卿、少卿各一員為提督，遂改隸太常。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Hongzhi, one additional Director and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were first appointed as Supervisors, and the offices were then placed under that court.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi year 7 added a supervising Director and Vice Director from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transferred the bureaus to its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，裁卿，止少卿一人。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign the supervising Director was cut, leaving only one Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing the supervising directorship was abolished, leaving a single Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 按太常寺卿在南京者，多由科目。

translations.literal: As a rule, Directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing were mostly drawn from the examination track.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, Nanjing directors of the court were mostly examination graduates.

sentences.zh: 北寺自永樂間用樂舞生，累資升至寺卿，甚或加禮部侍郎、尚書掌寺，後多沿襲。

translations.literal: At the northern court, since the Yongle era music-and-dance students were used, promoted by seniority to Director, and some even concurrently held Vice Minister or Minister of Rites posts while directing the court—a practice largely continued afterward.
translations.idiomatic: At the northern capital, since Yongle, music-and-dance students had risen by seniority to director, some even concurrently serving as vice minister or minister of rites—a pattern that long persisted.

sentences.zh: 至隆慶初，乃重推科甲出身者補任。

translations.literal: Only at the beginning of Longqing were graduates of the examination track again strongly favored for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Not until early Longqing were examination graduates again strongly favored for these posts.

sentences.zh: 譯字生，明初甚重。

translations.literal: Translation Students were highly valued in early Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Translation students were highly prized in early Ming.

sentences.zh: 與考者，與鄉、會試額科甲一體出身。

translations.literal: Those who took the examinations received the same metropolitan and palace examination quotas and jinshi standing as others.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sat the exams shared provincial and metropolitan quotas and received jinshi standing on the same terms.

sentences.zh: 後止為雜流。

translations.literal: Later they were reduced to miscellaneous-track status only.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were relegated to the miscellaneous service track only.

sentences.zh: 其在館者，升轉皆在鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: Those serving in the bureaus were promoted and transferred entirely within the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Staff in the bureaus were promoted and transferred entirely within the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 卿一人，從三品少卿二人，正五品寺丞二人，從六品其屬，典簿廳，典簿二人，從七品錄事一人，從八品大官、珍羞、良醞、掌醢四署，各署正一人，從六品署丞四人，從七品監事四人，從八品司牲司，大使一人，從九品副使一人，後革司牧局，大使一人，從九品，嘉靖七年革。

translations.literal: One Director at rank 3b; two Vice Directors at rank 5a; two Assistant Directors at rank 6b. Subordinates: Registry with two Registrars at rank 7b; one Recorder at rank 8b; four offices—Grand Cuisine, Delicacies, Fine Brew, and Condiments—each with one Director at rank 6b, four Assistant Directors at rank 7b, and four Supervisors at rank 8b; Office of Victims with one Chief Envoy at rank 9b and one Vice Envoy (later the Herds Office with one Chief Envoy at rank 9b was abolished in the seventh year of Jiajing).
translations.idiomatic: One Director at rank 3b, two Vice Directors at 5a, and two Assistant Directors at 6b. Subordinates included a registry (two registrars at 7b), one recorder at 8b, and four offices—Grand Cuisine, Delicacies, Fine Brew, and Condiments—each with a director at 6b, four deputies at 7b, and four supervisors at 8b; an Office of Victims with chief and vice envoys at 9b (the Herds Office, also rank 9b, was abolished in Jiajing year 7).

sentences.zh: 銀庫，大使一人。

translations.literal: Silver Treasury, with one Chief Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The Silver Treasury had one chief envoy.

sentences.zh: 卿，掌祭享、宴勞、酒醴、膳羞之事，率少卿、寺丞官屬，辨其名數，會其出入，量其豐約，以聽於禮部。

translations.literal: The Director oversaw sacrificial offerings, banquets of reward, wine, and food provisions, leading Vice Directors, Assistant Directors, and subordinates to distinguish items and quantities, tally receipts and disbursements, gauge abundance or scarcity, and report to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Director oversaw sacrificial provisions, reward banquets, wine, and food, directing his vice directors and staff to track items, receipts, and disbursements, gauge supply, and report to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，同太常省牲；

translations.literal: For all sacrifices, jointly with the Court of Imperial Sacrifices inspected victims;
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices it joined the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in inspecting victims;

sentences.zh: 天子親祭，進飲福受胙；

translations.literal: when the Son of Heaven sacrificed in person, presented the blessing-cup and received sacrificial meat;
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor sacrificed in person, presented the blessing cup and received the sacrificial meat;

sentences.zh: 薦新，循月令獻其品物；

translations.literal: for seasonal new offerings, presented items according to the monthly ordinances;
translations.idiomatic: for seasonal new offerings, supplied items according to the monthly calendar;

sentences.zh: 喪葬供奠饌。

translations.literal: for funerals and burials supplied offerings and feast foods.
translations.idiomatic: and for funerals supplied offerings and feast foods.

sentences.zh: 所用牲、果、菜物，取之上林苑；

translations.literal: Victims, fruit, and vegetables used were drawn from the Imperial Parks;
translations.idiomatic: Victims, fruit, and vegetables came from the Imperial Parks;

sentences.zh: 不給，市諸民，視時估十加一，其市直季支天財庫。

translations.literal: if insufficient, purchased from the populace at ten percent above current market price, with payments disbursed quarterly from the Heavenly Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: shortfalls were bought from the market at ten percent above the going rate, paid quarterly from the Heavenly Treasury.

sentences.zh: 四方貢獻果鮮廚料，省納惟謹。

translations.literal: Fruit, fresh produce, and kitchen supplies presented as tribute from all quarters were received and stored with scrupulous care.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute fruit, fresh produce, and kitchen stores from all regions were received and stored with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 器皿移工部及募工兼作之，歲省其成敗。

translations.literal: Vessels and utensils were referred to the Ministry of Works and contracted labor for joint production; each year their completion was reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels were ordered through the Ministry of Works and hired labor, with annual review of what was finished.

sentences.zh: 凡筵宴酒食及外使、降人，俱差其等而供給焉。

translations.literal: For all banquets, food, and drink, as well as foreign envoys and surrendered persons, supplies were graded by rank and provided accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Banquets, foreign envoys, and surrendered persons all received provisions graded to their rank.

sentences.zh: 傳奉宣索，籍記而覆奏之。

translations.literal: Imperial orders transmitted for requisition were recorded and reported back.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial requisitions were logged and reported back to court.

sentences.zh: 監以科道官一員，察其出入，糾禁其奸弊。

translations.literal: One censorial official supervised receipts and disbursements and checked abuses.
translations.idiomatic: A censorial official monitored receipts and disbursements and checked abuses.

sentences.zh: 歲四月至九月，凡御用物及祭祀之品皆用冰。

translations.literal: From the fourth through the ninth month, all imperial supplies and sacrificial items used ice.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth through the ninth month, imperial and sacrificial provisions were kept on ice.

sentences.zh: 大官，供祭品宮膳、節令筵席、蕃使宴犒之事。

translations.literal: Grand Cuisine supplied sacrificial offerings, palace meals, seasonal banquets, and feasts for foreign envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Cuisine supplied sacrificial offerings, palace meals, seasonal banquets, and envoy feasts.

sentences.zh: 珍羞，供宮膳餚核之事。

translations.literal: Delicacies supplied palace meals and delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Delicacies supplied palace dishes and delicacies.

sentences.zh: 良醞，供酒醴之事。

translations.literal: Fine Brew supplied wine and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Fine Brew supplied wine and spirits.

sentences.zh: 掌醢，供餳、油、醯、醬、梅、鹽之事。

translations.literal: Condiments supplied malt sugar, oil, vinegar, sauce, preserved plums, and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Condiments supplied malt sugar, oil, vinegar, sauces, preserved plums, and salt.

sentences.zh: 司牲養牲，視其肥瘠而蠲滌之。

translations.literal: The Office of Victims raised victims, judging their fatness or leanness and purifying them.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Victims raised sacrificial animals, judging their condition and purifying them.

sentences.zh: 司牧亦如之。

translations.literal: The Herds Office did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The Herds Office did the same.

sentences.zh: 初，吳元年置宣徽院，設院使，正三品同知，正四品院判，正五品典簿。

translations.literal: Originally, in the first year of the Wu reign era the Court of Palace Provisions was established, with a Commissioner at rank 3a, Vice Commissioner at rank 4a, Assistant Commissioner at rank 5a, and Registrar at rank 5a.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu 1 the Court of Palace Provisions was set up with a commissioner at rank 3a, vice commissioner at 4a, assistant commissioner at 5a, and registrar at 5a.

sentences.zh: 正七品以尚食、尚醴二局隸之。

translations.literal: rank 7a. The Offices of Imperial Food and Imperial Wine were subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: at rank 7a. The Offices of Imperial Food and Imperial Wine were placed under it.

sentences.zh: 局設大使，從六品，副使，從七品洪武元年改為光祿寺，設光祿卿，正四品少卿，正五品寺丞，正六品主簿。

translations.literal: Each office had a Chief Envoy at rank 6b and Vice Envoy at rank 7b. In Hongwu 1 it was renamed the Court of Imperial Entertainments, with Director at rank 4a, Vice Director at rank 5a, Assistant Director at rank 6a, and Chief Clerk at rank 6a.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau had a chief envoy at rank 6b and vice envoy at 7b. Hongwu year 1 renamed it the Court of Imperial Entertainments with a director at 4a, vice director at 5a, assistant director at 6a, and chief clerk at 6a.

sentences.zh: 正八品所屬尚食等局，又移太常司供需庫隸之。

translations.literal: rank 8b. Subordinate offices such as Imperial Food were placed under it, and the supply depot of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was also transferred to its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: at rank 8b. Subordinate bureaus such as Imperial Food came under it, and the supply depot of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was transferred as well.

sentences.zh: 局庫官品仍舊。

translations.literal: The ranks of bureau and depot officials remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau and depot ranks were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二年，設直長四人，遇百官賜食御前者，則令供事。

translations.literal: In year 2, four Duty Chiefs were established; when officials of all ranks were granted food before the emperor, they were ordered to provide service.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2 added four duty chiefs to serve whenever officials were granted food in the emperor's presence.

sentences.zh: 四年，置法酒庫。

translations.literal: In year 4 the Statutory Wine Depot was established.
translations.idiomatic: Year 4 established the Statutory Wine Depot.

sentences.zh: 設內酒坊大使，從八品，副使，從九品。

translations.literal: An Inner Brewery was established with Chief Envoy at rank 8b and Vice Envoy at rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: An Inner Brewery was set up with a chief envoy at rank 8b and vice envoy at 9b.

sentences.zh: 八年，改寺為司，升卿秩，卿從三品，少卿從四品。

translations.literal: In year 8 the court was renamed a bureau and the Director's rank was raised: Director to rank 3b, Vice Director to rank 4b.
translations.idiomatic: Year 8 renamed the court a bureau and raised ranks: the director to 3b and the vice director to 4b.

sentences.zh: 以寺丞為司丞，從六品主簿為典簿，從七品增設錄事。

translations.literal: Assistant Directors became bureau assistants at rank 6b; Chief Clerks became Registrars at rank 7b; Recorders were added at rank 8b.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant directors became bureau assistants at 6b, chief clerks became registrars at 7b, and recorders were added at 8b.

sentences.zh: 從八品又置所屬大官、珍羞、良醞、掌醢四署，每署令一人，從六品丞一人，從七品監事一人。

translations.literal: rank 8b. Four subordinate offices were also established—Grand Cuisine, Delicacies, Fine Brew, and Condiments—each with one Director at rank 6b, one Assistant Director at rank 7b, and one Supervisor at rank 8b.
translations.idiomatic: at rank 8b. Four subordinate offices were added—Grand Cuisine, Delicacies, Fine Brew, and Condiments—each with a director at 6b, deputy at 7b, and supervisor at 8b.

sentences.zh: 從八品孳牧所，大使一人，從九品副使一人。

translations.literal: rank 8b. A Breeding Herds Office, with one Chief Envoy and one Vice Envoy at rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: at rank 8b. A Breeding Herds Office with one chief envoy and one vice envoy at 9b.

sentences.zh: 未入流十年，定光祿司散官品秩。

translations.literal: In year 10, ranks of honorary posts for the Bureau of Imperial Entertainments were fixed for officials outside the regular hierarchy.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10 fixed the honorary ranks for Bureau of Imperial Entertainments officials outside the regular hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 時所用光祿司官，或內官，或流官，或庖人，出身不同，同授散官。

translations.literal: At the time the Bureau of Imperial Entertainments employed inner-court officials, regular officials, or cooks; though their origins differed, all were granted the same honorary ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the bureau drew on inner-court staff, regular officials, and cooks; despite their different backgrounds, all received the same honorary ranks.

sentences.zh: 至是定，內官除授者，照內官散官給授。

translations.literal: Now it was fixed: those appointed from inner-court service received honorary ranks according to the inner-court scale.
translations.idiomatic: The rule was now fixed: appointees from the inner court received honorary ranks on the inner-court scale.

sentences.zh: 流官除授者，照文官散官給授。

translations.literal: Those appointed from the regular hierarchy received honorary ranks according to the civil-official scale.
translations.idiomatic: Appointees from the regular civil service received honorary ranks on the civil-official scale.

sentences.zh: 庖人除授者，卿從三品，授尚膳大夫；

translations.literal: For cooks appointed to office: a Director at rank 3b received the title Grand Master of Imperial Provisions;
translations.idiomatic: Cooks appointed as director at rank 3b received the title Grand Master of Imperial Provisions;

sentences.zh: 少卿正五品，授奉膳大夫；

translations.literal: a Vice Director at rank 5a received the title Grand Master of Court Provisions;
translations.idiomatic: vice director at rank 5a received Grand Master of Court Provisions;

sentences.zh: 司丞從六品，授司膳郎；

translations.literal: a Bureau Assistant at rank 6b received the title Gentleman of Provisions;
translations.idiomatic: bureau assistant at rank 6b received Gentleman of Provisions;

sentences.zh: 客署丞從七品，授掌膳郎；

translations.literal: a Guest Office Assistant at rank 7b received the title Gentleman in Charge of Provisions;
translations.idiomatic: guest office assistant at rank 7b received Gentleman in Charge of Provisions;

sentences.zh: 監事從八品，授執膳郎。

translations.literal: a Supervisor at rank 8b received the title Gentleman Attending Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: and supervisor at rank 8b received Gentleman Attending Provisions.

sentences.zh: 尋罷各局庫，置司牲司，又改孳牧所為司牧司。

translations.literal: Soon all bureaus and depots were abolished; the Bureau of Victims was established, and the Breeding Herds Office was renamed the Bureau of Herds.
translations.idiomatic: Soon every bureau and depot was abolished, a Bureau of Victims was set up, and the Breeding Herds Office became the Bureau of Herds.

sentences.zh: 後為司牧局。

translations.literal: Later it became the Herds Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: It was later renamed the Herds Bureau.

sentences.zh: 三十年，復改為光祿寺，官制仍舊。

translations.literal: In year 30 it was again renamed the Court of Imperial Entertainments, with the official structure restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Year 30 restored the name Court of Imperial Entertainments and the former official structure.

sentences.zh: 少卿已定正五品。

translations.literal: The Vice Director's rank had already been fixed at 5a.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director's rank had already been fixed at 5a.

sentences.zh: 建文中，升少卿、寺丞品秩。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, the ranks of Vice Director and Assistant Director were raised.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen the ranks of vice director and assistant director were raised.

sentences.zh: 少卿升四品，寺丞升五品。

translations.literal: The Vice Director was raised to rank 4; the Assistant Director to rank 5.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director rose to rank 4 and the assistant director to rank 5.

sentences.zh: 增設司圃所，改司牲司為孳牲所。

translations.literal: A Garden Produce Office was added, and the Bureau of Victims was renamed the Breeding Victims Office.
translations.idiomatic: A Garden Produce Office was added and the Bureau of Victims became the Breeding Victims Office.

sentences.zh: 升其品級成祖復舊制。

translations.literal: Their ranks were raised; the Yongle Emperor restored the former system.
translations.idiomatic: Their ranks were raised; the Yongle Emperor then restored the former system.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，裁四署冗員。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhengtong reign, redundant staff in the four offices were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong year 6 cut redundant staff in the four subordinate offices.

sentences.zh: 先是，光祿卿奈享以供應事繁，奏增各署官，至是復奏裁之。

translations.literal: Previously Director Nai Xiang, finding provisioning duties overwhelming, had memorialized to increase staff in each office; now he memorialized again to cut them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Director Nai Xiang had found provisioning work overwhelming and memorialized to add staff in each office; he now memorialized to cut them back.

sentences.zh: 裁署正四人，署丞五人，監事七人。

translations.literal: Four office directors, five assistant directors, and seven supervisors were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Four office directors, five assistant directors, and seven supervisors were abolished.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，革司牧局。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Jiajing reign, the Herds Bureau was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year 7 abolished the Herds Bureau.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，添設銀庫大使一人。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Wanli reign, one chief envoy for the Silver Depot was added.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli year 2 added one chief envoy for the Silver Depot.

sentences.zh: 太僕寺。

translations.literal: The Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 卿一人，從三品少卿二人，正四品，正德十一年增設一人。

translations.literal: One Director at rank 3b; two Vice Directors at rank 4a—in the eleventh year of the Zhengde reign one more was added.
translations.idiomatic: One director at rank 3b; two vice directors at rank 4a; Zhengde year 11 added a third vice director.

sentences.zh: 寺丞四人。

translations.literal: Four Assistant Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Four assistant directors.

sentences.zh: 正六品其屬，主簿廳，主簿一人。

translations.literal: Rank 6a subordinates: the Registry, with one Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates at rank 6a included a Registry with one chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 從七品常盈庫，大使一人。

translations.literal: The Full Stores Depot at rank 7b, with one Chief Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The Full Stores Depot at rank 7b had one chief envoy.

sentences.zh: 所轄，各牧監，監正一人，正九品監副一人，從九品錄事一人。

translations.literal: Under its jurisdiction, each Pasture Supervisor had one Supervisor-in-Chief at rank 9a, one Deputy Supervisor at rank 9b, and one Recorder at rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: Each pasture under its jurisdiction had one supervisor-in-chief at rank 9a, one deputy supervisor at 9b, and one recorder at 9b.

sentences.zh: 後監正、監副、錄事俱革。

translations.literal: Later the Supervisor-in-Chief, Deputy Supervisor, and Recorder were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later the supervisor-in-chief, deputy supervisor, and recorder were all abolished.

sentences.zh: 各羣，羣長一人。

translations.literal: Each herd had one Herd Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Each herd had one herd chief.

sentences.zh: 後革

translations.literal: Later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: These posts were later abolished.

sentences.zh: 卿，掌牧馬之政令，以聽於兵部。

translations.literal: The Director oversaw policies for horse-rearing and took direction from the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The director oversaw horse-rearing policy and reported to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 少卿一人佐寺事，一人督營馬，一人督畿馬。

translations.literal: One Vice Director assisted in court affairs, one supervised camp horses, and one supervised capital-region horses.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director assisted in court business, one supervised camp horses, and one supervised horses in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 寺丞分理京衛、畿內及山東、河南六郡孳牧、寄牧馬匹。

translations.literal: Assistant Directors divided responsibility for breeding and entrusted horses in the capital guards, capital region, and the six prefectures of Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant directors divided responsibility for breeding and entrusted horses in the capital guards, the capital region, and the six prefectures of Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 濟南、兗州、東昌、開封、彰德、衛輝。

translations.literal: Jinan, Yanzhou, Dongchang, Kaifeng, Zhangde, and Weihui.
translations.idiomatic: namely Jinan, Yanzhou, Dongchang, Kaifeng, Zhangde, and Weihui.

sentences.zh: 凡軍民孳牧，視其丁產，授之種馬。

translations.literal: For all military and civilian breeding, stallions were allotted according to household labor and property.
translations.idiomatic: For all military and civilian breeding, breeding stock was allotted according to household labor and means.

sentences.zh: 牡十之二，牝十之八，為一羣。

translations.literal: Two males and eight females in ten formed one herd.
translations.idiomatic: A herd consisted of two stallions and eight mares in every ten head.

sentences.zh: 南方以四牝一牡為羣。

translations.literal: In the south a herd was four females to one male.
translations.idiomatic: In the south a herd was four mares to one stallion.

sentences.zh: 歲徵其駒，曰備用馬，齊其力以給將士。

translations.literal: Each year foals were levied as reserve horses; their strength was assessed to supply officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Each year foals were levied as reserve horses, graded for strength, and issued to officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 將士足，則寄牧於畿內府州縣，肥瘠登耗，籍其毛齒而時閱之。

translations.literal: When troops had enough mounts, horses were entrusted to prefectures and counties within the capital region; fatness, leanness, gain, and loss were registered by coat and teeth and periodically inspected.
translations.idiomatic: When troops had sufficient mounts, horses were entrusted to prefectures and counties in the capital region; condition and numbers were registered by coat and teeth and inspected regularly.

sentences.zh: 三歲偕御史一人印烙，選其健良而汰其羸劣。

translations.literal: At age three, together with one censor, they were branded; the strong and sound were selected and the weak culled.
translations.idiomatic: At age three, together with a censor, horses were branded; the strong and sound were kept and the weak culled.

sentences.zh: 其草場已墾成田者，歲斂其租金，災祲則出之以佐市馬。

translations.literal: Where pasture had been reclaimed as farmland, rent was collected yearly; in years of disaster the funds were drawn from it to help purchase horses on the market.
translations.idiomatic: Where pasture had been converted to farmland, rent was collected yearly; in years of disaster those funds helped purchase horses on the market.

sentences.zh: 其賠償折納，則徵馬金輸兵部。

translations.literal: For compensation commuted to payment, horse silver was levied and delivered to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When compensation was commuted to cash payment, horse silver was levied and remitted to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 主簿典勾省文移。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk managed document checking and filing.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk managed document review and filing.

sentences.zh: 大使典貯庫馬金。

translations.literal: The Chief Envoy managed storage of horse silver in the depot.
translations.idiomatic: The chief envoy managed the depot's horse-silver reserves.

sentences.zh: 初，洪武四年置羣牧監於答答失裏營所，隨水草利便立官署，專司牧養。

translations.literal: Initially, in Hongwu year 4 a herd pasture supervisor was established at the Dadashili garrison; offices were set up wherever grass and water were advantageous, exclusively managing horse rearing.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 4 a herd pasture supervisor was first established at the Dadashili garrison, with offices placed wherever grass and water were favorable to manage horse rearing.

sentences.zh: 六年，更置羣牧監於滁州，旋改為太僕寺，秩從三品，設卿、少卿、寺丞，又設首領官知事、主簿各一人。

translations.literal: In year 6 it was moved to Chuzhou; it was soon renamed the Court of the Imperial Stud at rank 3b, with Director, Vice Director, and Assistant Director, plus one Recorder and one Chief Clerk as chief officers.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6 moved it to Chuzhou and soon renamed it the Court of the Imperial Stud at rank 3b, with director, vice director, and assistant director, plus one recorder and one chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 七年，增設牧監、羣官二十七處，隸太僕寺。

translations.literal: In year 7 twenty-seven pasture supervisors and herd offices were added, subordinate to the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7 added twenty-seven pasture supervisors and herd offices under the court.

sentences.zh: 尋定羣牧監品秩。

translations.literal: Soon ranks for herd pasture supervisors were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks for herd pasture supervisors were soon fixed.

sentences.zh: 令，正五品，丞，正六品，鎮撫，從六品，羣頭十人、吏目一人，省注。

translations.literal: Director, rank 5a; Deputy, rank 6a; Pacification Commissioner, rank 6b; ten herd heads and one clerk—with notation abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: Director at 5a, deputy at 6a, pacification commissioner at 6b, ten herd heads and one clerk—the record abbreviates the rest.

sentences.zh: 十年，增置滁陽等各牧監及所屬各羣。

translations.literal: In year 10 various pasture supervisors such as Chuyang and their subordinate herds were added.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10 added pasture supervisors such as Chuyang and their subordinate herds.

sentences.zh: 改牧監令、丞為監正、監副。

translations.literal: Pasture supervisor Directors and Deputies were renamed Supervisor-in-Chief and Deputy Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture directors and deputies were renamed supervisor-in-chief and deputy supervisor.

sentences.zh: 監正，從八品，監副，正九品，禦良，從九品。

translations.literal: Supervisor-in-Chief, rank 8b; Deputy Supervisor, rank 9a; Imperial Groom, rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor-in-chief at rank 8b, deputy supervisor at 9a, imperial groom at 9b.

sentences.zh: 後又定監正為正九品。

translations.literal: Later the Supervisor-in-Chief was fixed at rank 9a.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor-in-chief was later fixed at rank 9a.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，定滁陽等十二牧監，每監設監正一人，監副二人，錄事一人。

translations.literal: In year 22 twelve pasture supervisors including Chuyang were fixed; each had one Supervisor-in-Chief, two Deputy Supervisors, and one Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Year 22 fixed twelve pasture supervisors including Chuyang; each had one supervisor-in-chief, two deputy supervisors, and one recorder.

sentences.zh: 來安等一百二十七羣，每羣設羣長一人。

translations.literal: One hundred twenty-seven herds including Lai'an; each had one Herd Chief.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred twenty-seven herds including Lai'an each had one herd chief.

sentences.zh: 初設羣副二人，至是革。

translations.literal: Initially two Deputy Herd Chiefs were established; now they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Two deputy herd chiefs had initially been appointed; they were now abolished.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，增置江東、當塗二牧監及所屬各羣。

translations.literal: In year 23 two pasture supervisors, Jiangdong and Dangtu, and their subordinate herds were added.
translations.idiomatic: Year 23 added the Jiangdong and Dangtu pasture supervisors and their subordinate herds.

sentences.zh: 又罷烏衣等五十四羣，改置永安等七羣，定為牧監十四，滁陽、大興、香泉、儀真、定遠、天長、長淮、江都、句容、溧陽、江東、溧水、當塗、舒城。

translations.literal: Fifty-four herds including Wuyi were abolished and seven including Yong'an were established; fourteen pasture supervisors were fixed: Chuyang, Daxing, Xiangquan, Yizhen, Dingyuan, Tianchang, Changhuai, Jiangdu, Jurong, Liyang, Jiangdong, Lishui, Dangtu, and Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-four herds including Wuyi were abolished and seven including Yong'an were established; fourteen pasture supervisors were fixed at Chuyang, Daxing, Xiangquan, Yizhen, Dingyuan, Tianchang, Changhuai, Jiangdu, Jurong, Liyang, Jiangdong, Lishui, Dangtu, and Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 羣九十有七。

translations.literal: Ninety-seven herds in all.
translations.idiomatic: There were ninety-seven herds in all.

sentences.zh: 大勝關、柏子、騮興、保寧、草堂五羣，隸滁陽監。

translations.literal: Dashengguan, Baizi, Liuxing, Baoning, and Caotang—five herds under the Chuyang Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Dashengguan, Baizi, Liuxing, Baoning, and Caotang herds under Chuyang Pasture.

sentences.zh: 永安、如皋、沿海、保全、朝陽、永昌、安定七羣，隸大興監。

translations.literal: Yong'an, Rugao, Yanhai, Baoquan, Chaoyang, Yongchang, and Anding—seven herds under the Daxing Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an, Rugao, Yanhai, Baoquan, Chaoyang, Yongchang, and Anding herds under Daxing Pasture.

sentences.zh: 大錢、銅城、永豐、龍勝、龍山、永寧、新安、慶安、襄安九羣，隸香泉監。

translations.literal: Daqian, Tongcheng, Yongfeng, Longsheng, Longshan, Yongning, Xin'an, Qing'an, and Xiang'an—nine herds under the Xiangquan Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Daqian, Tongcheng, Yongfeng, Longsheng, Longshan, Yongning, Xin'an, Qing'an, and Xiang'an herds under Xiangquan Pasture.

sentences.zh: 華陽、壽寧、廣陵、善應四羣，隸儀真監。

translations.literal: Huayang, Shouning, Guangling, and Shanying—four herds under the Yizhen Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Huayang, Shouning, Guangling, and Shanying herds under Yizhen Pasture.

sentences.zh: 龍江、龍安、萬勝、龍泉四羣，隸定遠監。

translations.literal: Longjiang, Long'an, Wansheng, and Longquan—four herds under the Dingyuan Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Longjiang, Long'an, Wansheng, and Longquan herds under Dingyuan Pasture.

sentences.zh: 天長、懷德、招信、得勝、武安五羣，隸天長監。

translations.literal: Tianchang, Huaide, Zhaoxin, Desheng, and Wu'an—five herds under the Tianchang Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Tianchang, Huaide, Zhaoxin, Desheng, and Wu'an herds under Tianchang Pasture.

sentences.zh: 長安、白石、荊山、南山、團山、草平六羣，隸長淮監。

translations.literal: Chang'an, Baishi, Jingshan, Nanshan, Tuanshan, and Caoping—six herds under the Changhuai Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an, Baishi, Jingshan, Nanshan, Tuanshan, and Caoping herds under Changhuai Pasture.

sentences.zh: 萬甯、廣生、萬驥、順德、大興、驥寧、崇德七羣，隸江都監。

translations.literal: Wanning, Guangsheng, Wanji, Shunde, Daxing, Jining, and Chongde—seven herds under the Jiangdu Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Wanning, Guangsheng, Wanji, Shunde, Daxing, Jining, and Chongde herds under Jiangdu Pasture.

sentences.zh: 句容、易風、仍信、福胙、通德、承佩、上容、政仁、練塘、壽安十羣，隸句容監。

translations.literal: Jurong, Yifeng, Rengxin, Fuzuo, Tongde, Chengpei, Shangrong, Zhengren, Liantang, and Shou'an—ten herds under the Jurong Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Jurong, Yifeng, Rengxin, Fuzuo, Tongde, Chengpei, Shangrong, Zhengren, Liantang, and Shou'an herds under Jurong Pasture.

sentences.zh: 舉福、從山、明義、永定、福賢、崇來、永城、永泰、奉安九羣，隸溧陽監。

translations.literal: Jufu, Congshan, Mingyi, Yongding, Fuxian, Chonglai, Yongcheng, Yongtai, and Feng'an—nine herds under the Liyang Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Jufu, Congshan, Mingyi, Yongding, Fuxian, Chonglai, Yongcheng, Yongtai, and Feng'an herds under Liyang Pasture.

sentences.zh: 開寧、泉水、惟政、清化、神泉、新亭、長泰、光澤八羣，隸江東監。

translations.literal: Kaining, Quanshui, Weizheng, Qinghua, Shenquan, Xinting, Changtai, and Guangze—eight herds under the Jiangdong Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Kaining, Quanshui, Weizheng, Qinghua, Shenquan, Xinting, Changtai, and Guangze herds under Jiangdong Pasture.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳、仙壇、立信、歸政、豐慶、安興、遊山、永寧八羣，隸溧水監。

translations.literal: Yifeng, Xiantan, Lixin, Guizheng, Fengqing, Anxing, Youshan, and Yongning—eight herds under the Lishui Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng, Xiantan, Lixin, Guizheng, Fengqing, Anxing, Youshan, and Yongning herds under Lishui Pasture.

sentences.zh: 石城、永保、化洽、姑熟、繁昌、多福、丹陽、德政八羣，隸當塗監。

translations.literal: Shicheng, Yongbao, Huaqia, Gushu, Fanchang, Duofu, Danyang, and Dezheng—eight herds under the Dangtu Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng, Yongbao, Huaqia, Gushu, Fanchang, Duofu, Danyang, and Dezheng herds under Dangtu Pasture.

sentences.zh: 棗林、海亭、伏龍、龍河、會龍、九龍、萬龍七羣，隸舒城監。

translations.literal: Zaolin, Haiting, Fulong, Longhe, Huilong, Jiulong, and Wanlong—seven herds under the Shucheng Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Zaolin, Haiting, Fulong, Longhe, Huilong, Jiulong, and Wanlong herds under Shucheng Pasture.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，悉罷羣牧監，以其馬隸有司牧養。

translations.literal: In year 28 all herd pasture supervisors were abolished; their horses were placed under local officials for rearing.
translations.idiomatic: Year 28 abolished all herd pasture supervisors and placed their horses under local officials for rearing.

sentences.zh: 三十年，置行太僕寺於北平，秩如太僕寺。

translations.literal: In year 30 an itinerant Court of the Imperial Stud was established at Beiping, with rank equal to the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Year 30 established an itinerant Court of the Imperial Stud at Beiping with rank equal to the main court.

sentences.zh: 建文中，升寺丞品秩，舊六品，升五品。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, Assistant Director rank was raised from the former rank 6 to rank 5.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen the assistant director's rank was raised from the former 6 to 5.

sentences.zh: 又改其首領官職名，增設錄事，及典廄、典牧二署，壚肅騻等十八羣，滁陽等八牧監，龍山等九十二羣。

translations.literal: The titles of chief officers were changed, Recorders were added, and the Stable Management and Herd Management offices were established, with eighteen herds including Lu, Su, and Juan, eight pasture supervisors including Chuyang, and ninety-two herds including Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chief officer titles were changed, recorders were added, and the Stable Management and Herd Management offices were set up, with eighteen herds including Lu, Su, and Juan, eight pasture supervisors including Chuyang, and ninety-two herds including Longshan.

sentences.zh: 成祖復舊制。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor restored the former system.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor restored the former system.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，改北平行太僕寺為北京行太僕寺。

translations.literal: In Yongle 1 the Beiping itinerant Court of the Imperial Stud was renamed the Beijing itinerant Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle year 1 renamed the Beiping itinerant court the Beijing itinerant Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 十八年定都北京，遂以行太僕寺為太僕寺。

translations.literal: In year 18, when the capital was fixed at Beijing, the itinerant court became the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was fixed at Beijing in year 18, the itinerant court became the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，復稱北京行太僕寺。

translations.literal: In Hongxi 1 it was again called the Beijing itinerant Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxi year 1 restored the name Beijing itinerant Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，定為太僕寺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhengtong reign it was fixed as the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong year 6 fixed it as the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 其舊在滁州者，改為南京太僕寺。

translations.literal: The former court at Chuzhou was renamed the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The former court at Chuzhou became the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 寺丞，初置四人。

translations.literal: Assistant Directors: initially four were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant directors: four were initially appointed.

sentences.zh: 正統中，又增八人，共十二人，以一人領京衛，一人領順德、廣平二府，一人領開封、衛輝、彰德三府，九人分領順天、保定、真定、河間、永平、大名、濟南、兗州、東昌九府孳牧、寄牧各馬匹。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign eight more were added for twelve in all: one oversaw capital guards, one oversaw Shunde and Guangping prefectures, one oversaw Kaifeng, Weihui, and Zhangde, and nine divided among Shuntian, Baoding, Zhending, Hejian, Yongping, Daming, Jinan, Yanzhou, and Dongchang for breeding and entrusted horses.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengtong eight more were added for twelve in all: one oversaw the capital guards, one Shunde and Guangping, one Kaifeng, Weihui, and Zhangde, and nine divided Shuntian, Baoding, Zhending, Hejian, Yongping, Daming, Jinan, Yanzhou, and Dongchang for breeding and entrusted horses.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年革四人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Hongzhi reign four posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi year 6 cut four posts.

sentences.zh: 正德九年復增一人，專領寄牧之事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Zhengde reign one more was added, exclusively overseeing entrusted rearing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde year 9 added one post devoted exclusively to entrusted rearing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年又革三人，共六人分領，三年更代，而以寄牧者令府州縣兼理。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Jiajing reign three more were cut; six divided responsibilities on three-year rotation, and entrusted rearing was handled jointly by prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year 8 cut three more, leaving six on three-year rotation; entrusted rearing was assigned to prefectures and counties to manage jointly.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年又革三人，止設三人，以一人提督庫藏兼協理京邊，二人分理東西二路各馬政。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Longqing reign three more were cut, leaving only three: one supervised the depot and coordinated capital-frontier affairs, and two divided east and west routes for horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing year 3 cut three more, leaving only three: one supervised the depot and coordinated capital-frontier affairs, and two divided horse administration on the eastern and western routes.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: The Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 卿一人，正四品左、右少卿各一人，從五品左、右寺丞各一人。

translations.literal: One Director at rank 4a; Left and Right Vice Directors, one each at rank 5b; Left and Right Assistant Directors, one each at rank 6b.
translations.idiomatic: One director at rank 4a; left and right vice directors at rank 5b; left and right assistant directors at rank 6b.

sentences.zh: 從六品其屬，主簿廳，主簿一人。

translations.literal: Rank 6b subordinates: the Registry, with one Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates at rank 6b included a Registry with one chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 從八品司儀、司賓二署，各署丞一人，正九品鳴贊四人，從九品，後增設五人。

translations.literal: At rank 8b, the Ceremonies and Guests offices, each with one Assistant Director at rank 9a; four Masters of Announcement at rank 9b—later increased by five.
translations.idiomatic: At rank 8b, the Ceremonies and Guests offices each had one assistant director at 9a; four masters of announcement at 9b were later increased by five.

sentences.zh: 序班五十人。

translations.literal: Fifty Ushers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty ushers.

sentences.zh: 從九品。

translations.literal: Rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: at rank 9b.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十六年革八人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign eight posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year 36 cut eight posts.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十一年復設六人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of the Wanli reign six posts were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli year 11 restored six posts.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚，掌朝會、賓客、吉凶儀禮之事。

translations.literal: The Court of State Ceremonial oversaw court assemblies, foreign guests, and auspicious and inauspicious ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The court oversaw court assemblies, foreign guests, and ritual for auspicious and inauspicious occasions.

sentences.zh: 凡國家大典禮、郊廟、祭祀、朝會、宴饗、經筵、冊封、進曆、進春、傳制、奏捷，各供其事。

translations.literal: For all great state ceremonials—suburban and temple rites, sacrifices, court assemblies, banquets, imperial lectures, investitures, presentation of the calendar, presentation of spring, promulgation of edicts, and reports of victory—each supplied its proper service.
translations.idiomatic: For great state ceremonials, suburban and temple rites, sacrifices, court assemblies, banquets, imperial lectures, investitures, calendar and spring offerings, promulgation of edicts, and victory reports, it supplied the appropriate service for each.

sentences.zh: 外吏朝覲，諸蕃入貢，與夫百官使臣之復命、謝恩，若見若辭者，並鴻臚引奏。

translations.literal: When outside officials came for audience, various foreign states paid tribute, and officials and envoys reported back or offered thanks—whether for audience or leave-taking—the Court of State Ceremonial led presentation and memorialized all alike.
translations.idiomatic: For audiences by outside officials, tribute missions, and ministers' and envoys' reports of mission, thanksgiving audiences, presentations, and farewells, the court led presentation and memorialized to the throne.

sentences.zh: 歲正旦、上元、重午、重九、長至賜假、賜宴，四月賜字扇、壽縷，十一月賜戴暖耳，陪祀畢，頒胙賜，皆贊百官行禮。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, the Lantern Festival, Double Fifth, Double Ninth, and the winter solstice it granted leave and banquets; in the fourth month it granted inscribed fans and longevity threads; in the eleventh month it granted ear-warmers; after collateral sacrifices it distributed sacrificial meat—it directed all officials in ritual throughout.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, the Lantern Festival, Double Fifth, Double Ninth, and the winter solstice it arranged leave and banquets; in the fourth month inscribed fans and longevity threads; in the eleventh month ear-warmers; after collateral sacrifices it distributed sacrificial portions—all occasions on which it directed officials in ritual.

sentences.zh: 司儀，典陳設、引奏，外吏來朝，必先演儀於寺。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies managed arrangements and leading memorials; when outside officials came for audience, ritual was first rehearsed at the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies managed arrangements and presenting memorials; outside officials rehearsed ritual at the court before audience.

sentences.zh: 司賓，典外國朝貢之使，辨其等而教其拜跪儀節。

translations.literal: The Master of Guests managed envoys from foreign states paying tribute, distinguished their ranks, and taught them bowing and kneeling etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Guests managed foreign tribute envoys, distinguished their ranks, and instructed them in bowing and kneeling etiquette.

sentences.zh: 鳴贊，典贊儀禮。

translations.literal: The Master of Announcement managed announcement ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Announcement directed ritual announcements.

sentences.zh: 凡內贊、通贊、對贊、接贊、傳贊鹹職之。

translations.literal: All duties of inner announcement, general announcement, paired announcement, receiving announcement, and relayed announcement fell to this office.
translations.idiomatic: It handled all duties of inner, general, paired, receiving, and relayed announcement.

sentences.zh: 序班，典侍班、齊班、糾儀及傳贊。

translations.literal: Ushers managed attendance formation, lining up ranks, correcting ritual, and relayed announcement.
translations.idiomatic: Ushers managed attendance formation, lining up ranks, correcting ceremonial order, and relayed announcements.

sentences.zh: 初，吳元年置侍儀司，秩從五品。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the first year of Wu the Court Attendance Office was established, at rank 5b.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, in Wu 1 the Court Attendance Office was established at rank 5b.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年定侍儀使，從七品引進使，正八品奉班都知，正九品通贊、通事舍人，從九品俱為七品以下官。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 4 the Court Attendance Commissioner was fixed at rank 7b; the Presenting Commissioner at rank 8a; the Attendance Director at rank 9a; Masters of Announcement and Secretariat Interpreters at rank 9b—all were officials below rank 7.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu year 4 fixed the Court Attendance Commissioner at rank 7b, the Presenting Commissioner at 8a, the Attendance Director at 9a, and Masters of Announcement and Secretariat Interpreters at 9b—all posts below rank 7.

sentences.zh: 九年，改為殿庭儀禮司，設使一人，正七品副三人，正八品丞奉一人，從八品鳴贊二人，正九品序班十六人，從九品九關通事使一人，正八品副六人。

translations.literal: In year 9 it was changed to the Hall Ceremonial Office, with one Director at rank 7a, three Vice Directors at rank 8a, one Attendant at rank 8b, two Masters of Announcement at rank 9a, sixteen Ushers at rank 9b, one Nine-Pass Interpreter Commissioner at rank 9b, and six Vice Commissioners at rank 8a.
translations.idiomatic: Year 9 renamed it the Hall Ceremonial Office: one director (7a), three vice directors (8a), one attendant (8b), two masters of announcement (9a), sixteen ushers (9b), one Nine-Pass Interpreter Commissioner (9b), and six vice commissioners (8a).

sentences.zh: 從八品十三年，改使為司正，分左、右司副各一人，增序班至四十四人，革承奉，增設司儀四人。

translations.literal: Rank 8b; in year 13 the Director was changed to Supervisor, with Left and Right Vice Supervisors one each, Ushers increased to forty-four, Attendants abolished, and four Masters of Ceremonies added.
translations.idiomatic: At rank 8b; year 13 renamed the director Supervisor, appointed one left and one right vice supervisor, raised ushers to forty-four, abolished attendants, and added four masters of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，增設左、右司丞四人。

translations.literal: In year 22, four Left and Right Assistant Supervisors were added.
translations.idiomatic: Year 22 added four left and right assistant supervisors.

sentences.zh: 正九品三十年，始改為鴻臚寺，升秩正四品，設官六十二員。

translations.literal: Rank 9a; in year 30 it was first changed to the Court of State Ceremonial, rank raised to 4a, and sixty-two posts established.
translations.idiomatic: At rank 9a; year 30 renamed it the Court of State Ceremonial, raised its rank to 4a, and established sixty-two posts.

sentences.zh: 卿以下員數、品級如前所列。

translations.literal: Posts and ranks from the Director downward were as listed above.
translations.idiomatic: Posts and ranks from the director down matched the listing above.

sentences.zh: 又設外夷通事隸焉。

translations.literal: Foreign interpreters were also established and placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign interpreters were also placed under it.

sentences.zh: 建文中，升少卿以下品秩。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, ranks from Vice Director downward were raised.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwen, ranks from the vice director down were raised.

sentences.zh: 少卿升正五品，寺丞升正六品。

translations.literal: Vice Directors were raised to rank 5a; Assistant Directors to rank 6a.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors rose to rank 5a and assistant directors to 6a.

sentences.zh: 又改其首領官職名，與鳴贊、序班皆升品級。

translations.literal: Its chief officers' titles were also changed, and Masters of Announcement and Ushers all received higher ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Chief officers' titles were changed, and masters of announcement and ushers all received higher ranks.

sentences.zh: 罷司儀、司賓二署，而以行人隸鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: The Ceremonies and Guests offices were abolished, and Receptionists were placed under the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonies and Guests offices were abolished and receptionists placed under the court.

sentences.zh: 成祖初，悉復舊制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongle reign, everything was restored to the former system.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongle, the former system was fully restored.

sentences.zh: 尚寶司。

translations.literal: The Imperial Seals Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Seals Office.

sentences.zh: 卿一人，正五品少卿一人，從五品司丞三人。

translations.literal: One Director at rank 5a; one Vice Director at rank 5b; three Assistant Directors
translations.idiomatic: One director at rank 5a; one vice director at rank 5b; three assistant directors

sentences.zh: 正六品。

translations.literal: at rank 6a.
translations.idiomatic: at rank 6a.

sentences.zh: 吳元年但設一人，後增二人。

translations.literal: In Wu 1 only one was appointed; later two were added.
translations.idiomatic: Wu year 1 appointed only one; two were added later.

sentences.zh: 掌寶璽、符牌、印章，而辨其所用。

translations.literal: It managed imperial seals, tally plaques, and official seals, and distinguished their uses.
translations.idiomatic: It managed imperial seals, tally plaques, and official seals and determined their proper use.

sentences.zh: 寶二十有四。

translations.literal: There were twenty-four imperial seals.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-four imperial seals.

sentences.zh: 舊寶十有七，嘉靖十八年增制者七。

translations.literal: Seventeen were old seals; seven were added in the eighteenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen were legacy seals; seven were added in Jiajing year 18.

sentences.zh: 曰：「皇帝奉天之寶」，為唐、宋傳璽，祀天地用之。

translations.literal: One was called "Seal Received from Heaven by the Emperor"; a Tang and Song heirloom, used for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: One, "Seal Received from Heaven by the Emperor," was a Tang and Song heirloom used for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 若詔與赦，則用「皇帝之寶。」；

translations.literal: For edicts and amnesties, the seal "Imperial Seal"
translations.idiomatic: Edicts and amnesties used the "Imperial Seal"

sentences.zh: 冊封、賜勞，則用「皇帝行寶。」；

translations.literal: for investiture and rewarding service, the seal "Imperial Traveling Seal"
translations.idiomatic: investiture and rewards for service used the "Imperial Traveling Seal"

sentences.zh: 詔親王、大臣及調兵，則用「皇帝信寶。」；

translations.literal: for edicts to princes, ministers, and troop mobilization, the seal "Imperial Trust Seal"
translations.idiomatic: edicts to princes and ministers and orders to mobilize troops used the "Imperial Trust Seal"

sentences.zh: 上尊號，則用「皇帝尊親之寶。」；

translations.literal: for bestowing honorific titles, the seal "Imperial Seal Honoring the Parent"
translations.idiomatic: bestowing honorific titles used the "Imperial Seal Honoring the Parent"

sentences.zh: 諭親王，則用「皇帝親親之寶」。

translations.literal: To instruct princes, the seal "Imperial Seal of Kinship" was used.
translations.idiomatic: Instructions to princes used the "Imperial Seal of Kinship."

sentences.zh: 其「天子之寶」，以祀山川、鬼神；

translations.literal: The "Heaven's Son Seal" was used for sacrifices to mountains, rivers, and spirits;
translations.idiomatic: The "Heaven's Son Seal" served sacrifices to mountains, rivers, and spirits;

sentences.zh: 「天子行寶」，以封外國及賜勞；

translations.literal: the "Heaven's Son Traveling Seal" for sealing to foreign states and rewarding service;
translations.idiomatic: the "Heaven's Son Traveling Seal" for investitures abroad and service rewards;

sentences.zh: 「天子信寶」，以招外服及徵發。

translations.literal: the "Heaven's Son Trust Seal" for summoning border domains and mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: the "Heaven's Son Trust Seal" for summoning border domains and mobilizing forces.

sentences.zh: 詔用「制誥之寶。」；

translations.literal: Edicts used the seal "Seal of Proclamations and Decrees"
translations.idiomatic: Edicts used the "Seal of Proclamations and Decrees"

sentences.zh: 敕用「敕命之寶。」；

translations.literal: commands used the seal "Seal of Commands"
translations.idiomatic: Imperial commands used the "Seal of Commands"

sentences.zh: 獎勵臣工，用「廣運之寶。」；

translations.literal: to reward officials, the seal "Seal of Broad Influence"
translations.idiomatic: Rewards to officials used the "Seal of Broad Influence"

sentences.zh: 敕諭朝覲官，用「敬天勤民之寶」。

translations.literal: Commands instructing officials coming for audience used the "Seal of Revering Heaven and Diligently Serving the People."
translations.idiomatic: Instructions to officials attending court used the "Seal of Revering Heaven and Diligently Serving the People."

sentences.zh: 若「御前之寶」，「表章經史之寶」，「欽文之寶」，則圖書文史等用之。

translations.literal: The "Seal Before the Throne," "Seal for Petitions on the Classics and Histories," and "Seal of Imperial Documents" were used for books, writings, and historical records.
translations.idiomatic: The "Seal Before the Throne," "Seal for Petitions on the Classics and Histories," and "Seal of Imperial Documents" served books, writings, and historical matters.

sentences.zh: 世宗增制，為「奉天承運大明天子寶」，為「大明受命之寶」，為「巡狩天下之寶」，為「垂訓之寶」，為「命德之寶」，為「討罪安民之寶」，為「敕正萬民之寶。」。

translations.literal: The Jiajing Emperor added seven: "Great Ming Heaven's Son Seal, Mandate Received," "Great Ming Seal of Received Mandate," "Seal for Imperial Tours," "Seal of Lasting Instruction," "Seal of Mandated Virtue," "Seal for Punishing Crime and Settling the People," and "Seal for Correcting All the People."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor added seven: "Great Ming Heaven's Son Seal, Mandate Received," "Great Ming Seal of Received Mandate," "Seal for Imperial Tours," "Seal of Lasting Instruction," "Seal of Mandated Virtue," "Seal for Punishing Crime and Settling the People," and "Seal for Correcting All the People."

sentences.zh: 太子之寶一，曰：「皇太子之寶」。

translations.literal: There was one Heir Apparent seal, called "Seal of the Crown Prince."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had one seal, the "Seal of the Crown Prince."

sentences.zh: 凡寶之用，必奏請而待發。

translations.literal: Whenever a seal was used, memorial had to be submitted and await issuance.
translations.idiomatic: Use of any seal required memorial submission and awaiting issuance.

sentences.zh: 每大朝會，本司官二員，以寶導駕，俟升座，各置寶於案，立待殿中。

translations.literal: At each great court assembly, two officers of this office guided the imperial carriage with the seals; when the emperor ascended the throne, each placed a seal on its stand and stood waiting in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At each great court assembly, two officers of the office guided the procession with the seals; after the emperor ascended the throne, each placed a seal on its stand and waited in the hall.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，捧寶分行，至中極殿，置案而出。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, they bore the seals in separate rows to the Hall of Central Supremacy, placed them on stands, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended, they carried the seals separately to the Hall of Central Supremacy, set them on stands, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 駕出幸，則奉以從焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor went on tour, they bore them in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, they accompanied him bearing the seals.

sentences.zh: 歲終，移欽天監，擇日和香物入水，洗寶於皇極門。

translations.literal: At year's end they notified the Directorate of Astronomy, chose an auspicious day, and with incense and offerings entered water to wash the seals at the Gate of Imperial Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end they coordinated with the Directorate of Astronomy, chose an auspicious day, and with incense and offerings washed the seals at the Gate of Imperial Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 籍奏一歲用寶之數。

translations.literal: They registered and memorialized the number of seal uses for the year.
translations.idiomatic: They recorded and memorialized how many times each seal had been used that year.

sentences.zh: 凡請寶、用寶、捧寶、隨寶、洗寶、繳寶，皆與內官尚寶監俱。

translations.literal: All matters of requesting seals, using seals, bearing seals, accompanying seals, washing seals, and returning seals were handled jointly with the inner-court Imperial Seals Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Requesting, using, bearing, accompanying, washing, and returning seals were all handled jointly with the inner-court Imperial Seals Directorate.

sentences.zh: 凡金牌之號五，以給勳戚侍衛之扈從及班直者、巡朝者、夜宿衛者：曰仁，其形龍，公、侯、伯、駙馬都尉佩之；

translations.literal: There were five types of gold tally plaques, issued to meritorious kin bodyguards for escort, shift duty, palace patrol, and night guard: Ren (Benevolence), dragon-shaped, worn by dukes, marquises, earls, and imperial sons-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: Five gold tally types served meritorious kin bodyguards on escort, standing duty, palace patrol, and night guard: Ren (Benevolence), dragon-shaped, for dukes, marquises, earls, and imperial sons-in-law;

sentences.zh: 曰義，其形虎，勳衛指揮佩之；

translations.literal: Yi (Righteousness), tiger-shaped, worn by meritorious guard commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Yi (Righteousness), tiger-shaped, for meritorious guard commanders;

sentences.zh: 曰禮，其形麟，千戶佩之；

translations.literal: Li (Propriety), unicorn-shaped, worn by chiliarchs;
translations.idiomatic: Li (Propriety), unicorn-shaped, for chiliarchs;

sentences.zh: 曰智，其形獅，百戶佩之；

translations.literal: Zhi (Wisdom), lion-shaped, worn by centurions;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi (Wisdom), lion-shaped, for centurions;

sentences.zh: 曰信，其形祥雲，將軍佩之。

translations.literal: Xin (Trust), auspicious-cloud-shaped, worn by generals.
translations.idiomatic: Xin (Trust), auspicious-cloud-shaped, for generals.

sentences.zh: 半字銅符之號四，以給巡城寺衛官：曰承，曰東，曰西，曰北。

translations.literal: Four half-character bronze tallies served city-patrol guard officers: Cheng, East, West, and North.
translations.idiomatic: Four half-character bronze tallies identified city-patrol guard officers: Cheng, East, West, and North.

sentences.zh: 巡者左半，守者右半，合契而點察焉。

translations.literal: Patrollers held the left half and guards the right; the halves were matched to inspect.
